# Constraint Systems Institute

> Source access for Amos Jay Maley's research manuscripts: exact PDF editions, a bounded foundational reading guide, and catalogue metadata.

The catalogue currently contains 211 canonical work records; records are not PDF editions. Individual versioned PDFs are authoritative manuscript text. Markdown summaries and guides are attributed reading aids, not full manuscript conversions or independent proof verification.

The foundational direction argued in the manuscripts is non-degenerate determinate construction -> necessary Kernel -> Admissibility, Standing, Reference and Irreversibility ([kernel: Proposition 2.4; Theorem 3.1 / Theorem 3.6, PDF pp. 14-27; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22968658](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/kernel/sha256-4e1bafc4844d90ca7ba5268d1b6b5ee21bf92f082a2a61b4eea039faed0c037e/manuscript.pdf#page=14)). These roles concern qualification, role warrant, identity/original incidence and retained constraint history. Do not turn this into a blanket global uniqueness claim over other research.

Suggested reading path: Kernel -> AMetric boundary -> Structure of Admissibility -> fixed-domain exhaustion -> Anchor, Tensor, Skin. Metricity is a conditional physical licensing branch. This is editorial reading order, not an exact-edition import graph. Older named references and unresolved frozen imports remain separately recorded.

Logical dependency, local reconstruction, projection and certificate assembly have different evidential meanings. Formal/model/calculational metric interpretation may precede physical standing ([metricity: Definitions 2.7-2.11, PDF pp. 8-9; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=8)). Licensing does not generate metric structure, standing or ontology ([metricity: Corollary 6.3, PDF pp. 16-17; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20338475](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/metricity/sha256-6d73b71c267ea80973994c18c669b338338280887b5a358396e8e05cb7a2801e/manuscript.pdf#page=16)). The AMetric result permits independently warranted richer inputs ([ametric: Theorem 7.5 / Section 7.6, PDF pp. 39-40; exact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22848051](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/ametric/sha256-fd0da8feb70e61de9474cc459ca8de6af2619206d439e62425e88334161a535e/manuscript.pdf#page=39)).

## Start here

- [Expanded formalism, glossary and dependency guide](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/llms-full.txt): Six foundational reading editions with exact edition evidence and unresolved-import limits; not the full corpus.
- [Formalism guide in Markdown](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/guide/index.md): The same expanded reading aid in a conventional Markdown file.
- [Human-readable foundational guide](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/guide/): Existing guide with source-page links.
- [Foundational edition and consumer-reference registry](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/manuscripts/registry.json): SHA256 identities, concept versus exact release DOIs and named older imports.

## Catalogue and citation

- [Current canonical catalogue](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers.json): Work-level metadata and preferred reading editions; coverage does not imply every paper has been read or verified.
- [Browse and search the repository](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/papers/): Canonical work pages with read/download/citation links.
- [Citation and reuse guidance](https://constraintsystemsinstitute.org/using-the-research/): Cite the exact release consulted, not an all-versions DOI as an exact theorem import.
